html:
The Siege of Vicksburg lasted from 18 May to 4 July 1863 at Vicksburg, a town on the Mississippi River in the state of Mississippi, United States. The Union army of General Ulysses S. Grant forced a Confederate army of about 30,000 under General John Pemberton to surrender.

Vicksburg stood on high bluffs, and its guns closed the river to Union ships. It was the main link between the two halves of the Confederacy. Attacks from the north had failed in the swamps. In April 1863 Grant marched down the far bank, crossed the river south of the town and cut loose from his supplies. In 17 days he won five battles and shut Pemberton inside. Two direct assaults failed, so Grant dug in. For 47 days his guns and the navy's gunboats shelled the town. People sheltered in caves, and food ran out. Pemberton surrendered on 4 July.

It came one day after the Union victory at Gettysburg. The Union now held the whole river, and the Confederacy was cut in two. The campaign made Grant's name. In 1864 Lincoln put him in command of all Union armies in the American Civil War.
